speaker: john_shakespeare
text: The stall bundles on the hurdle, Will, and out of the sun when they are tied. Tomorrow is Thursday, and Joan will not sell a bundle she has not tied herself.

speaker: joan_shakespeare
text: If I let you tie them, the hedging-gloves come out on top and the fine stitching goes at the bottom of the pannier.

speaker: richard_shakespeare
text: Eighteen pair for the stall. The parings go back in the basket. Hamnet, keep thy thumb off the alum if thou art in the shop.

speaker: hamnet_shakespeare
text: I am on the windfalls under the wall. The bruised ones go to the tub. The sound ones go on the shelf.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: This one has a wasp in the side. Which basket takes a wasp?

speaker: hamnet_shakespeare
text: The pig-bucket by the gate, after the wasp is out. Twenty sound ones, when I am done, and the soft ones are not a count I will swear to yet.

speaker: anne_shakespeare
text: Thy grandfather gives thee every scrap that wants paring, and then wonders why a pocket smells of the lime-pit.

speaker: john_shakespeare
text: A boy's pocket should have a scrap in it. What else will he mend a hinge with? The stall is the work. The apples are the boy's.

speaker: richard_shakespeare
text: Carry the tied bundles into the shop when the sun is on the hurdle. The wrist dries if they sit.

speaker: joan_shakespeare
text: The rush-gatherer from the lane, Anne, for the dips ordered on Monday.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Stay. I have my belt on. What is the reckoning?

speaker: john_shakespeare
text: Put thy hand down, Will. This is the house's ordering, not a tavern in Bishopsgate. Anne has the bag at her girdle. Let her pay her own door.

speaker: anne_shakespeare
text: I have it here. Come to the step. We will see the bundle before anyone talks of pence.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: My hand is off the belt.

speaker: john_shakespeare
text: A man does not ask a guest for kitchen pence in his own yard, even when the guest is his son. The belt is for a sum you mean. This is not that sum.

speaker: richard_shakespeare
text: The cuff on the top pair wants three stitches before market. Joan has the waxed thread.

speaker: joan_shakespeare
text: Set it by the window. I will stitch it when the rushes are in.

speaker: hamnet_shakespeare
text: Tomorrow after the Cross you are coming up past the Rother Market. You promised on Sunday.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I promised on Sunday. I am yours after the stall, and not before Joan has sold a glove.

speaker: john_shakespeare
text: Half past nine at the stall first. I will be on a ladder when the ladders go up. You will find me by the noise.

speaker: anne_shakespeare
text: The rushes are in, and they are paid for, and the coin is not a story. Bring the apple-basket in, Hamnet, before the hens find it.

speaker: hamnet_shakespeare
text: Twenty sound ones on the shelf. Twelve for the bucket. The wasp-apple is in neither, because the wasp is still in it.

speaker: joan_shakespeare
text: Ten hours in a field once a summer, and we shall hear of his shoulders till Michaelmas.

speaker: john_shakespeare
text: Let him talk of them. It keeps his hands on a hurdle. The door is Anne's, and it is done.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The door is hers. I am carrying bundles into the shade, and I am not opening the belt for a rush.
